```{r}
# ==========================================================
#  Bid-Rent Curve — Median Rent vs. Distance from Financial District
# ==========================================================
# Requires: tidycensus, tidyverse, sf, geosphere, scales, ggplot2
# install.packages(c("tidycensus","tidyverse","sf","geosphere","scales","ggplot2"))

library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(geosphere)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)

# -------------------------
# 1) PARAMETERS / API KEY
# -------------------------
state_fips <- "06"   # California
county_fips <- "075" # San Francisco County
year <- 2023
var_rent <- "B25064_001"   # Median gross rent
center_lonlat <- c(-122.3988, 37.7913)  # Pine & Market (Financial District)

# -------------------------
# 2) DOWNLOAD ACS TRACT DATA
# -------------------------
message("Downloading ACS tract median rent (this may take a few seconds)...")
rent_sf <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  state = state_fips,
  county = county_fips,
  variables = var_rent,
  year = year,
  geometry = TRUE,
  cache_table = TRUE
) %>%
  rename(median_rent = estimate) %>%
  select(GEOID, NAME, median_rent, geometry) %>%
  st_transform(4326)

if (nrow(rent_sf) == 0) stop("No tract data returned — check your Census API key and connection.")

# -------------------------
# 3) COMPUTE DISTANCE (km)
# -------------------------
rent_sf <- rent_sf %>%
  mutate(
    centroid = st_centroid(geometry),
    lon = st_coordinates(centroid)[,1],
    lat = st_coordinates(centroid)[,2],
    distance_km = distHaversine(cbind(lon, lat), matrix(center_lonlat, ncol = 2)) / 1000
  )

# -------------------------
# 4) FILTER TO <= 12 km
# -------------------------
rent_sf_core <- rent_sf %>% filter(distance_km <= 12)

if (nrow(rent_sf_core) == 0) stop("No tracts found within 12 km — check center coordinates or units.")

# -------------------------
# 5) FIT LINEAR MODEL
# -------------------------
model_lm <- lm(median_rent ~ distance_km, data = rent_sf_core)

# Print detailed results
print(summary(model_lm))

# Neat equation output
coefs <- coef(model_lm)
intercept <- round(coefs[1], 2)
slope <- round(coefs[2], 2)
r2 <- round(summary(model_lm)$r.squared, 3)

cat("\nLinear fit (printed separately):\n")
cat("Median_Rent = ", intercept, ifelse(slope < 0, "- ", "+ "), abs(slope),
    " * Distance_km\n", sep = "")
cat("R-squared: ", r2, "\n\n", sep = "")

# -------------------------
# 6) PLOT: Bid-Rent Scatter with LOESS + Linear Fit
# -------------------------
p_bid_rent <- ggplot(rent_sf_core, aes(x = distance_km, y = median_rent)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = median_rent), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "black", linewidth = 1.1) +  # LOESS curve
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#d73027", linewidth = 1.0, linetype = "dashed") +  # Linear fit
  scale_color_gradientn(
    colors = colorRampPalette(c(
      "#313695","#4575b4","#74add1","#abd9e9",
      "#fee090","#fdae61","#f46d43","#d73027","#a50026"
    ))(200),
    name = "Median Rent (USD)",
    labels = label_dollar()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Median Rent vs Distance from Financial District",
    subtitle = "Census tracts (ACS 2023). Distances measured from Market & Pine Sts.",
    x = "Distance from Financial District (km)",
    y = "Median Rent (USD)",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

# -------------------------
# 7) DISPLAY PLOT
# -------------------------
print(p_bid_rent)

```


```{r}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
library(scales)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Convert rent_sf to WGS84 and compute tract centroids
# ------------------------------------------------------------
rent_sf_ll <- st_transform(rent_sf, 4326) %>%
  mutate(
    centroid = st_centroid(geometry),
    lon = st_coordinates(centroid)[,1],
    lat = st_coordinates(centroid)[,2]
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Remove all non-mainland tracts (Farallon Islands, misc water polygons)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
rent_sf_mainland <- rent_sf_ll %>%
  filter(
    lon > -122.55,   # west boundary
    lon < -122.35,   # east boundary
    lat > 37.70,     # south boundary
    lat < 37.84      # north boundary
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Calculate dynamic breaks for rent values
# ------------------------------------------------------------
min_rent <- floor(min(rent_sf_mainland$median_rent, na.rm = TRUE) / 200) * 200
max_rent <- ceiling(max(rent_sf_mainland$median_rent, na.rm = TRUE) / 200) * 200
breaks <- seq(min_rent, max_rent, by = 200)

rainbow_colors <- colorRampPalette(c(
  "#313695", "#4575b4", "#74add1", "#abd9e9",
  "#fee090", "#fdae61", "#f46d43", "#d73027", "#a50026"
))(length(breaks) - 1)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Plot the rent map (MAINLAND ONLY)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
p_rent_clean <- ggplot(rent_sf_mainland) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = median_rent), color = "white", size = 0.05) +
  
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = rainbow_colors,
    breaks = breaks,
    labels = function(x) ifelse(x %% 400 == 0, dollar(x), ""),
    limits = c(min_rent, max_rent),
    name = "Median Gross Rent (USD)"
  ) +

  coord_sf(datum = NA, expand = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Median Rent by Census Tract — San Francisco",
    subtitle = "American Community Survey 2023",
    caption = "Each polygon = Census tract. Colors correspond to $200 rent intervals."
  ) +
  theme_map() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "Helvetica", size = 14),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.width = unit(3, "cm"),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.7, "cm"),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth = 20,
    barheight = 0.8,
    title.position = "top",
    title.hjust = 0.5
  ))

print(p_rent_clean)

```

```{r}
# --- SPATIAL MAP: Rent Growth (2018–2023) across SF Census Tracts ---
# install.packages(c("tidycensus", "tidyverse", "sf", "scales", "viridis"))

library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(scales)

# --- PARAMETERS ---
sf_state_fips <- "06"   # California
sf_county_fips <- "075" # San Francisco County
years <- c(2018, 2023)
var_rent <- "B25064_001"  # Median gross rent

# --- 1. Download ACS rent data with geometry for both years ---
acs_list <- map(years, function(y) {
  message("Fetching ACS ", y, " ...")
  get_acs(
    geography = "tract",
    state = sf_state_fips,
    county = sf_county_fips,
    variables = var_rent,
    year = y,
    geometry = TRUE,
    cache_table = TRUE
  ) %>%
    rename(median_rent = estimate) %>%
    select(GEOID, NAME, median_rent, geometry) %>%
    mutate(year = y)
})

sf_acs <- bind_rows(acs_list)

# --- 2. Split, join safely, and compute growth ---
rent_2018 <- sf_acs %>% 
  filter(year == 2018) %>% 
  select(GEOID, rent_2018 = median_rent, geometry)

rent_2023 <- sf_acs %>% 
  filter(year == 2023) %>% 
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  select(GEOID, rent_2023 = median_rent)

sf_growth <- rent_2018 %>%
  left_join(rent_2023, by = "GEOID") %>%
  mutate(
    rent_change = rent_2023 - rent_2018,
    rent_growth_pct = 100 * (rent_change / rent_2018)
  )

# --- 3. Trim outliers for clearer visualization ---
sf_growth <- sf_growth %>%
  mutate(rent_growth_pct = pmax(pmin(rent_growth_pct, 50), -50))

# --- 4. Plot map ---
p_map <- ggplot(sf_growth) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = rent_growth_pct), color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#d73027", mid = "white", high = "#1a9850",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-50, 50),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    name = "Rent Growth\n2018 → 2023"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Change in Median Gross Rent (2018–2023)",
    subtitle = "Census Tracts — San Francisco County, ACS 5-Year Estimates",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau, ACS 5-Year (B25064_001)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank()
  )

print(p_map)

```
```{r}
# --- Commute Time Map: San Francisco County ---
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)

# Load your dataset (update path if needed)
commute_data <- read_csv("Vital_Signs__Commute_Time_-_Tracts_20251106.csv")

# Convert to sf object using WKT geometry
commute_sf <- st_as_sf(commute_data, wkt = "geometry", crs = 4326)

# --- Filter for San Francisco County and remove outliers ---
sf_commute <- commute_sf %>%
  filter(
    str_to_lower(county) == "san francisco",
    !is.na(average_commute_time),
    average_commute_time > 0,
    average_commute_time <= 180  # cap at 3 hours
  )

# --- Define color breaks (5-minute increments up to 60) ---
breaks_labels <- seq(0, 60, by = 5)

# --- Create map ---
p_commute_sf <- ggplot(sf_commute) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = average_commute_time), color = "white", size = 0.08) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = c("#1a9850", "#fee08b", "#d73027"),  # green → yellow → red
    limits = c(0, 60),
    breaks = breaks_labels,
    labels = breaks_labels,
    name = "Mean Commute Time (minutes)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Commute Time (San Francisco, 2023)",
    subtitle = "Source: Vital Signs / U.S. Census Bureau",
    caption = "Each polygon represents a Census Tract"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth = 18,
    barheight = 0.8,
    title.position = "top",
    title.hjust = 0.5,
    label.position = "bottom",
    ticks = TRUE
  ))

# --- Display map ---
print(p_commute_sf)

```

```{r}
# ==========================================================
#  Commute Time vs. Distance from Financial District — SF Tracts
# ==========================================================
# Requires: tidyverse, sf, geosphere, ggplot2, scales
# install.packages(c("tidyverse","sf","geosphere","ggplot2","scales"))

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(geosphere)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 1) LOAD OR USE EXISTING SF COMMUTE DATA (from Vital Signs)
# ----------------------------------------------------------
# Assumes you already have `sf_commute` created with geometry and average_commute_time
# If not, read from your Vital Signs dataset:
# commute_data <- read_csv("Vital_Signs__Commute_Time_-_Tracts_20251106.csv")
# sf_commute <- st_as_sf(commute_data, wkt = "geometry", crs = 4326)

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 2) COMPUTE DISTANCE (km) FROM FINANCIAL DISTRICT
# ----------------------------------------------------------
center_coords <- c(-122.4014, 37.7901)  # Pine & Market
sf_commute <- sf_commute %>%
  mutate(
    centroid = st_centroid(geometry),
    lon = st_coordinates(centroid)[,1],
    lat = st_coordinates(centroid)[,2],
    distance_km = distHaversine(cbind(lon, lat), matrix(center_coords, ncol = 2)) / 1000
  )

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 3) FILTER: Within 12 km & realistic commute times (< 180 min)
# ----------------------------------------------------------
sf_commute_near <- sf_commute %>%
  filter(distance_km <= 12, average_commute_time <= 180, average_commute_time > 0)

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 4) FIT LINEAR MODEL
# ----------------------------------------------------------
lm_commute <- lm(average_commute_time ~ distance_km, data = sf_commute_near)
summary(lm_commute)

# Nicely print equation and R²
coefs <- coef(lm_commute)
intercept <- round(coefs[1], 2)
slope <- round(coefs[2], 2)
r2 <- round(summary(lm_commute)$r.squared, 3)

cat("\nLinear fit (printed separately):\n")
cat("Commute_Time = ", intercept, ifelse(slope < 0, "- ", "+ "), abs(slope),
    " * Distance_km\n", sep = "")
cat("R-squared: ", r2, "\n\n", sep = "")

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 5) SCATTERPLOT WITH LOESS + LINEAR MODEL
# ----------------------------------------------------------
p_commute_scatter <- ggplot(sf_commute_near, aes(x = distance_km, y = average_commute_time)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "#2b83ba", size = 2.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, color = "#1a9850", fill = "#fee08b", linewidth = 1.1) +  # LOESS
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#d73027", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1.0) +  # Linear fit
  labs(
    title = "Commute Time vs. Distance from Financial District",
    subtitle = "Census Tracts — San Francisco County",
    x = "Distance from Pine & Market (km)",
    y = "Average Commute Time (minutes)",
    caption = "Source: Vital Signs / ACS 2023"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5)
  )

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 6) DISPLAY PLOT
# ----------------------------------------------------------
print(p_commute_scatter)

```

```{r}
# ==========================================================
#   Average Building Stories by Census Tract — San Francisco
# ==========================================================
library(sf)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidycensus)
library(scales)

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Get San Francisco census tracts (geometry)
# ----------------------------------------------------------
sf_tracts <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  state = "06",
  county = "075",
  variables = "B01001_001",  # dummy variable to get geometry
  year = 2023,
  geometry = TRUE
) %>%
  select(GEOID, geometry)

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Load Building Footprints GeoJSON
# ----------------------------------------------------------
sf_buildings <- st_read("Building_Footprints.geojson")
sf_buildings <- st_make_valid(sf_buildings)

# (Optional) drop any empty geometries
sf_buildings <- sf_buildings[!st_is_empty(sf_buildings), ]

# Then reproject
sf_buildings <- st_transform(sf_buildings, st_crs(sf_tracts))

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Convert height (cm) → meters → stories
# ----------------------------------------------------------
sf_buildings <- sf_buildings %>%
  mutate(
    hgt_meancm = as.numeric(hgt_meancm),
    height_m = hgt_meancm / 100,
    stories = height_m / 3
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(stories) & stories > 0)

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Spatial join: assign buildings to census tracts
# ----------------------------------------------------------
buildings_by_tract <- st_join(sf_buildings, sf_tracts, join = st_intersects, left = FALSE)

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Aggregate mean stories per tract
# ----------------------------------------------------------
stories_by_tract <- buildings_by_tract %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(GEOID) %>%
  summarise(mean_stories = mean(stories, na.rm = TRUE))

# Join back to tract geometries
sf_stories_map <- sf_tracts %>%
  left_join(stories_by_tract, by = "GEOID")

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Plot: Average Building Stories by Census Tract
# ----------------------------------------------------------
p_stories <- ggplot(sf_stories_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = mean_stories), color = "white", size = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = rev(viridis::magma(9)),
    na.value = "gray90",
    labels = function(x) paste0(round(x, 1), " stories"),
    name = "Mean Stories"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Building Height (in Stories) by Census Tract — San Francisco",
    subtitle = "Derived from SF Building Footprints dataset (2025)",
    caption = "Source: data.sfgov.org / Building Footprints"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p_stories)

```
```{r}
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# -- Define city center (Pine & Market)
sf_center <- st_sfc(st_point(c(-122.4037, 37.7913)), crs = 4326)

# -- Reproject both to planar CRS (meters)
sf_stories_map_proj <- st_transform(sf_stories_map, 26910)  # NAD83 / UTM zone 10N (meters)
sf_center_proj <- st_transform(sf_center, 26910)

# -- Compute centroids of each tract and distance to city center
sf_stories_map_proj <- sf_stories_map_proj %>%
  mutate(
    centroid = st_centroid(geometry),
    distance_m = as.numeric(st_distance(centroid, sf_center_proj))
  )

# -- Restrict to tracts within 12 km
sf_stories_12km <- sf_stories_map_proj %>%
  filter(distance_m / 1000 <= 12)

# -- Create scatterplot with filtered data
p_dist <- ggplot(sf_stories_12km, aes(x = distance_m / 1000, y = mean_stories)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkred", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "darkgreen") +
  labs(
    x = "Distance from City Center (km)",
    y = "Average Building Stories per Tract",
    title = "Building Height vs. Distance from Downtown SF (≤12 km)",
    subtitle = "Dashed red = linear fit; Green = curved (LOESS) fit"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

print(p_dist)

# -- Save to Downloads
ggsave("C:/Users/robm7/Downloads/sf_building_height_vs_distance_12km.png", plot = p_dist, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 300)

# -- Compute linear model only on tracts within 12 km
lm_fit <- lm(mean_stories ~ I(distance_m / 1000), data = sf_stories_12km)
coef_lm <- coef(lm_fit)
cat("Linear Model (within 12 km): mean_stories = ", round(coef_lm[1], 3), " + ", round(coef_lm[2], 4), " * distance_km\n")
```

```{r}
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# --- 1. Define city center (Market & Pine)
sf_center <- st_sfc(st_point(c(-122.4037, 37.7913)), crs = 4326)

# --- 2. Reproject tracts to planar CRS (meters)
sf_pop_proj <- st_transform(sf_pop, 26910)
sf_center_proj <- st_transform(sf_center, 26910)

# --- 3. Compute centroids, distance, and area
sf_pop_proj <- sf_pop_proj %>%
  mutate(
    centroid = st_centroid(geometry),
    distance_m = as.numeric(st_distance(centroid, sf_center_proj)),
    area_km2 = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 1e6,
    pop_density = population / area_km2
  )

# --- 4. Filter tracts within 12 km and with valid population density
plot_df <- sf_pop_proj %>%
  filter(!is.na(pop_density) & distance_m / 1000 <= 12) %>%
  st_drop_geometry()

cat("Number of tracts included in scatterplot:", nrow(plot_df), "\n")

# --- 5. Scatterplot
p_density <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = distance_m / 1000, y = pop_density)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkred", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "darkgreen") +
  labs(
    x = "Distance from City Center (km)",
    y = "Population Density (people per km²)",
    title = "Population Density vs Distance from Downtown SF ",
    subtitle = "Dashed red = linear fit; Green = curved fit"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

print(p_density)

# --- 6. Save plot to Downloads
ggsave("C:/Users/robm7/Downloads/sf_population_density_vs_distance_12km.png",
       plot = p_density, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 300)

# --- 7. Linear regression
lm_fit <- lm(pop_density ~ I(distance_m / 1000), data = plot_df)
coef_lm <- coef(lm_fit)
cat("Linear Model (within 12 km): pop_density = ",
    round(coef_lm[1], 2), " + ", round(coef_lm[2], 2), " * distance_km\n")
```

```{r}
library(tidycensus)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)

# ----------------------------------------------------
# 1. PULL ACS POPULATION WITH GEOMETRY
# ----------------------------------------------------
sf_pop <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  state = "06",
  county = "075",
  variables = "B01001_001",
  geometry = TRUE,
  year = 2023
) %>%
  select(GEOID, NAME, population = estimate, geometry)

# ----------------------------------------------------
# 2. COMPUTE AREA AND POPULATION DENSITY
# ----------------------------------------------------
sf_pop_area <- sf_pop %>%
  mutate(
    area_m2 = st_area(geometry),
    area_mi2 = as.numeric(area_m2) / 2.58999e6,     # convert to square miles
    pop_density = population / area_mi2
  )

# ----------------------------------------------------
# 3. DEFINE CENTERPOINT (Pine & Market)
# ----------------------------------------------------
sf_center <- st_sfc(st_point(c(-122.4037, 37.7913)), crs = 4326)

# Project both to planar CRS (meters)
sf_pop_proj <- st_transform(sf_pop_area, 26910)
sf_center_proj <- st_transform(sf_center, 26910)

# ----------------------------------------------------
# 4. COMPUTE DISTANCE TO CENTER IN MILES
# ----------------------------------------------------
sf_pop_proj <- sf_pop_proj %>%
  mutate(
    centroid = st_centroid(geometry),
    distance_m = as.numeric(st_distance(centroid, sf_center_proj)),
    distance_mi = distance_m * 0.000621371
  )

# ----------------------------------------------------
# 5. CLEAN DATA FOR MODELING
# ----------------------------------------------------
df <- sf_pop_proj %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(!is.nan(pop_density), !is.infinite(pop_density)) %>%
  filter(distance_mi <= 12)   # restrict to 12 miles if desired

# ----------------------------------------------------
# 6. FIT A LOG-LINEAR DENSITY DECAY MODEL
# ----------------------------------------------------
# ln(density) = a + b * distance
# b ≈ percent change per mile
model <- lm(log(pop_density) ~ distance_mi, data = df)
summary(model)

b <- coef(model)[2]

# ----------------------------------------------------
# 7. INTERPRET THE DENSITY GRADIENT
# ----------------------------------------------------
density_gradient_percent <- (exp(b) - 1) * 100

cat("\n-----------------------------------------------\n")
cat("SF COUNTY DENSITY GRADIENT\n")
cat("-----------------------------------------------\n")
cat("Percent change in density per mile from center:\n")
cat("  ", round(density_gradient_percent, 2), "% per mile\n")
cat("-----------------------------------------------\n")
```

```{r}
library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(geosphere)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)

# -------------------------
# 1) PARAMETERS
# -------------------------
state_fips <- "06"   # California
county_fips <- "075" # San Francisco County
year <- 2023

var_rent  <- "B25064_001"  # Median gross rent
var_rooms <- "B25018_001"  # TRUE median number of rooms per unit

center_lonlat <- c(-122.3988, 37.7913)  # Pine & Market St.

# -------------------------
# 2) DOWNLOAD ACS MEDIAN RENT
# -------------------------
message("Downloading median rent...")
df_rent <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  state = state_fips,
  county = county_fips,
  variables = var_rent,
  year = year,
  geometry = TRUE
) %>%
  rename(median_rent = estimate) %>%
  select(GEOID, NAME, median_rent, geometry) %>%
  st_transform(4326)

# -------------------------
# 3) DOWNLOAD ACS MEDIAN ROOMS
# -------------------------
message("Downloading median rooms...")
df_rooms <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  state = state_fips,
  county = county_fips,
  variables = var_rooms,
  year = year,
  geometry = FALSE
) %>%
  rename(median_rooms = estimate) %>%
  select(GEOID, median_rooms)

# -------------------------
# 4) MERGE + COMPUTE DISTANCE
# -------------------------
rent_rooms_sf <- df_rent %>%
  left_join(df_rooms, by = "GEOID") %>%
  mutate(
    centroid = st_centroid(geometry),
    lon = st_coordinates(centroid)[,1],
    lat = st_coordinates(centroid)[,2],
    distance_km = distHaversine(cbind(lon, lat), matrix(center_lonlat, ncol = 2)) / 1000,
    rent_per_room = median_rent / median_rooms
  )

# -------------------------
# 5) FILTER WITHIN 12 KM
# -------------------------
rent_rooms_core <- rent_rooms_sf %>% filter(distance_km <= 12)

if(nrow(rent_rooms_core) == 0) stop("No tracts within 12 km — check coordinates.")

# -------------------------
# 6) LINEAR MODEL
# -------------------------
model_lm <- lm(rent_per_room ~ distance_km, data = rent_rooms_core)

print(summary(model_lm))

coefs <- coef(model_lm)
intercept <- round(coefs[1], 3)
slope <- round(coefs[2], 3)
r2 <- round(summary(model_lm)$r.squared, 3)

cat("\nLinear Model (printed separately):\n")
cat("Rent_per_room = ", intercept,
    ifelse(slope < 0, " - ", " + "), abs(slope),
    " * Distance_km\n", sep = "")
cat("R² = ", r2, "\n\n", sep = "")

# -------------------------
# 7) PLOT
# -------------------------
p_rent_per_room <- ggplot(rent_rooms_core, aes(x = distance_km, y = rent_per_room)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = rent_per_room), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "black", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#d73027",
              linewidth = 1.0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "#74add1", high = "#d73027",
                       name = "Rent per Room (USD)") +
  labs(
    title = "Bid Rent Curve: San Francisco",
    subtitle = "San Francisco Census Tracts ACS 2023",
    x = "Distance from Financial District (km)",
    y = "Bid Rent per Room (USD)",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

print(p_rent_per_room)

# Optional saving
# ggsave("rent_per_room_vs_distance.png", p_rent_per_room, width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300)

```
```{r}
library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(geosphere)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)

# -------------------------
# 1) PARAMETERS
# -------------------------
state_fips <- "06"   # California
county_fips <- "075" # San Francisco
year <- 2023

var_rooms <- "B25018_001"  # Median number of rooms per housing unit
center_lonlat <- c(-122.3988, 37.7913)  # Pine & Market

# -------------------------
# 2) DOWNLOAD ACS TRACT DATA
# -------------------------
message("Downloading ACS tract room counts (ACS 2023)...")
rooms_sf <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  state = state_fips,
  county = county_fips,
  variables = var_rooms,
  year = year,
  geometry = TRUE,
  cache_table = TRUE
) %>%
  rename(num_rooms = estimate) %>%
  select(GEOID, NAME, num_rooms, geometry) %>%
  st_transform(4326)

if (nrow(rooms_sf) == 0) stop("No ACS room data returned.")

# -------------------------
# 3) COMPUTE DISTANCE (km)
# -------------------------
rooms_sf <- rooms_sf %>%
  mutate(
    centroid = st_centroid(geometry),
    lon = st_coordinates(centroid)[,1],
    lat = st_coordinates(centroid)[,2],
    distance_km = distHaversine(cbind(lon, lat), matrix(center_lonlat, ncol = 2)) / 1000
  )

# -------------------------
# 4) FILTER TO <= 12 KM
# -------------------------
rooms_core <- rooms_sf %>% filter(distance_km <= 12)

if (nrow(rooms_core) == 0) stop("No tracts found within 12 km.")

# -------------------------
# 5) LINEAR MODEL
# -------------------------
model_lm <- lm(num_rooms ~ distance_km, data = rooms_core)
print(summary(model_lm))

coefs <- coef(model_lm)
intercept <- round(coefs[1], 3)
slope <- round(coefs[2], 3)
r2 <- round(summary(model_lm)$r.squared, 3)

cat("\nLinear model:\n")
cat("Num_Rooms = ", intercept,
    ifelse(slope < 0, " - ", " + "), abs(slope),
    " * Distance_km\n", sep = "")
cat("R² = ", r2, "\n\n", sep = "")

# -------------------------
# 6) PLOT: ROOMS VS DISTANCE
# -------------------------
p_rooms <- ggplot(rooms_core, aes(x = distance_km, y = num_rooms)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = num_rooms), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "black", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#d73027",
              linewidth = 1.0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "#74add1", high = "#d73027",
                       name = "Rooms per Unit") +
  labs(
    title = "Rooms per Dwelling vs Distance from Financial District",
    subtitle = "ACS 2023 — San Francisco Census Tracts",
    x = "Distance from Financial District (km)",
    y = "Median Number of Rooms",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

print(p_rooms)


```
